description: Gates the harness's OWN region-measuring instruments -- the six helpers in jas_dioxus/src/algorithms/polygon_metrics.rs and JasSwift/Sources/Algorithms/PolygonMetrics.swift (ring_signed_area, point_in_ring, point_in_polygon_set, polygon_set_area, is_ring_simple, all_rings_simple) that every boolean and boolean_normalize golden is expressed in. Those helpers used to be hand-copied into each roundtrip binary with nothing comparing the copies, so a drift in a measuring instrument could silently rewrite what the boolean families appear to prove. Ring sets here are inputs to the metrics directly: no boolean operation runs, so a red vector accuses the instrument and nothing else. Every expected number is derived independently (shoelace per ring, exact rectilinear cell decomposition, and a dense grid Riemann sum, cross-checked against the hand derivation in each vector's `derivation` field) -- never read back from either port. Areas are EVEN-ODD net areas: transcripts/BOOLEAN.md clause 1 makes a bare ring list mean even-odd-already-canonical, and clause 4 makes every generated boolean result declare even-odd.

vectors.name: single_square
vectors.derivation: One 10x10 square: shoelace 100, no overlap of any kind.

vectors.name: empty_set
vectors.derivation: No rings: every metric is the empty-sum identity.

vectors.name: two_point_ring_no_area
vectors.derivation: A 2-vertex ring bounds no region; shoelace is 0 and the scanline finds no band with a crossing.

vectors.name: edge_sharing_squares
vectors.derivation: Two 5x10 squares meeting along x=5. The shared edge has zero area, so the total is 50 + 50 = 100 -- touching is not overlap.

vectors.name: half_overlapping_squares
vectors.derivation: Two 10x10 squares overlapping in a 5x10 band: 100 + 100 - 2*50 = 100 (the symmetric difference is two 5x10 strips).

vectors.name: corner_overlap_inner_first_vertex
vectors.derivation: Two 10x10 squares overlapping in a 4x4 corner: 100 + 100 - 2*16 = 168. The second ring is listed from (6,6), which lies INSIDE the first.

vectors.name: corner_overlap_outer_first_vertex
vectors.derivation: Same two squares and the same cyclic vertex order as corner_overlap_inner_first_vertex, rotated to start at (16,6), which lies OUTSIDE the first ring. Area must be identical (168): the metric may not depend on which vertex a ring is listed from.

vectors.name: triple_overlap
vectors.derivation: Three 6x6 squares on a 3-unit grid. Coverage per 3x3 cell, reading the 3x3 block of cells with corners at multiples of 3: 1,2,1 / 1,3,2 / 0,1,1 (row order bottom to top). Six cells have ODD coverage, so the even-odd area is 6*9 = 54. Pins triple overlap, which pairwise subtraction alone would get wrong.

vectors.name: self_crossing_bowtie
vectors.derivation: One ring crossing itself at (5,5): two triangles of base 10 and height 5, so 25 + 25 = 50. Its shoelace sum is exactly 0, so signed area alone reports nothing.

vectors.name: square_triangle_overlap
vectors.derivation: A 10x10 square and a right triangle with legs 10 at (5,5). The triangle is x>=5, y>=5, x+y<=20; intersected with the square that is exactly the 5x5 block [5,10]x[5,10] (its far corner (10,10) sits on x+y=20). So 100 + 50 - 2*25 = 100. Non-axis-aligned: exercises the sloped-edge arm of the scanline.
